entry_points.text: Namespace descriptors under one magic offer no-data queries for owning user namespace, parent, type and owner, integer identifier translation between scopes, and mount-info fetch.

exports.text: Netlink sockets offer membership control, ring setup, strict checking and extended ack; extended errors carry message, offset, cookie and policy data.
Two read-style namespace operations return one 64-bit identifier to the caller for mount namespaces and for generic namespaces.

hazards.text: Some flag bits change meaning across dump, modify and acknowledgement uses; hook priority extremes reuse integer limits so ordering needs stable ties; nested attributes share type bits.
Status codes are discontinuous; timeout ceilings scale by HZ; fifo device negative one is a sentinel; namespace translation distinguishes from-scope versus in-scope direction.
Cached-only resolution can fail with retry when entries are absent; masked PCI fields require read-modify-write to preserve reserved bits.

invariants.text: Attribute families reserve zero for unspecified, list valid values, then define a public maximum as sentinel minus one so validators can size tables by that maximum.

Netlink framing aligns to four bytes; header length is aligned fixed size, iteration advances by aligned stored length, and a message is valid only when remaining length covers its header and stored length.

Low flag bits mark request, multipart, ack and echo; higher bits are reinterpreted by operation for dump versus modify; attribute types reserve top bits for nested and byte order; low message numbers are reserved controls.
Device-function codes pack a five-bit slot shifted left three with a three-bit function; slot extracts to a maximum of 31 and function to seven.
Mount records grow only by appending version-tagged members; namespace handle and identifier-request first sizes stay frozen while the leading size advertises current length.
Each user-visible header defines a single inclusion guard with no runtime behaviour.

state_machines.text: Dumps report sequence changes and server-side filtering, with overrun signalling loss and error carrying status.
Memory-mapped slots move from unused through reserved to valid, then to copy or skip as the consumer handles each frame.
Hotplug reports link up, link down, card present and card absent; power control holds current D-state with wake enable.

structs.text: Netlink address holds family, port identifier and multicast mask; message header holds length, type, flags, sequence and port; error container holds signed error plus embedded header with truncated payload.
Attribute header holds length and type; 32-bit bitfield holds value plus selector; mmap request holds block and frame geometry; mmap header holds status, length, group and credential identifiers.

Policy language separates invalid, flag, fixed-width integers, binary, strings, nested and bitfield; introspection records expected type with minima, maxima, length bounds and nested policy reference.

Objects form a numbered catalogue with table, name, type, data and handle; flowtables add offload and counter bits with hook and device set; trace reports carry table, chain, rule, verdict and snapshots with three traversal types.

Expressions use register plus attributes: FIB selects output with direction and mark flags; helper, timeout and expectation carry protocols and ports; OSF, synproxy, device and xfrm tune matching; generator and tunnel keys cover modulus, endpoints and encapsulation options.
IPv4 and IPv6 each expose five ordered hooks from pre-routing to post-routing; netlink protocol numbers identify subsystems up to a defined maximum link count.

NFS shares status codes, file kinds and limits across generations, with fixed v2 boundaries and modes, v3 access and capability flags, v4 bitmaps, delegations and exchange capabilities, plus program numbers and ports.

Handles are fixed opaque stores in v2 and length-prefixed stores in v3; mount arguments form a versioned record with flags and sizes; side ACL protocol uses presence masks; flush hints and diagnostic masks tune writeback and logging.

Namespace handle holds 64-bit identifier plus type and inode; identifier request adds size and owner; open config holds flags, mode and resolve controls; OOM adjustment spans negative to positive one thousand; mount-namespace info carries length, count and identifier.

Configuration space has classic and extended sizes with a standard header and multiple BARs; fixed offsets hold vendor, device, command, status and class; command enables IO, memory and mastering; status reports capabilities and errors; BAR low bits select space and type.

Subsystem identifiers precede capabilities; bridges encode bus numbers with parity and reset controls; CardBus mirrors bus numbers and controls; capabilities include power management; power control holds version and D-state; graphics and product-data registers cover AGP and vital data.

Initial namespaces use descending high inode numbers and sequential small identifiers with single-bit clone type codes; an all-ones marker selects the caller user namespace; PCI controller operations share a high-byte base with offsets for query, mmap mode and write combining.
